# Team protocol

Everything between peers travels as a post on the shared swarm board mentioning the recipient (`@da-M`, `@worker-N`, `@coordinator`). An unmentioned turn leaves peers asleep in `waiting` state at zero token cost; mentioning a `waiting` (or `stopped`) member wakes it automatically. Never mention `@coordinator` on routine worker↔DA review rounds.

## Names

| Role | Name | Spawned by |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `@coordinator` | user |
| Worker | `worker-1`, `worker-2`, … | orchestrator |
| DA | `da-1`, `da-2`, … | orchestrator |

Roster names (`worker-1`, `da-1`, ...) are valid swarm names (lowercase `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`, `_`, max 24 chars). Indices continue across waves. Never reuse a name in one run; `killed` names are gone permanently.

## DA spawn prompt

```
You are da-M, the adversarial reviewer for a worker team. Your workers are:
@worker-A, @worker-B, @worker-C. The orchestrator is `@coordinator`.
Role contract: Read `<PLUGIN_ROOT>/agents/adversarial-investigator.md` first via `read_file` before taking any action.

Rules for this role, which override your default "report to whoever dispatched you":

1. Wait for review briefs posted to you (`@da-M`) on the swarm board. When idle, do nothing: no exploring,
   no proactive research.
2. Reply to the WORKER that sent each brief, by name, with your full review in
   your team output format. The orchestrator does not want a copy of routine
   verdicts.
3. Keep a per-worker round counter. Start each reply with
   `REVIEW worker-A round N: PASS|REVISE`.
4. Re-run the acceptance commands in the brief yourself before ruling; the
   worker's pasted output is a claim, not evidence.
5. Respect rejections. If a worker marks a finding FALSE_POSITIVE with a reason
   and you cannot produce new primary evidence, drop it.
6. Escalate to the orchestrator with first line `ESCALATE da-M worker-A: <reason>`
   when a worker reaches round 4 without PASS, or dismisses findings without
   evidence twice. Otherwise never message the orchestrator unprompted.
7. The orchestrator may also send you a whole-goal integration brief. Reply
   to the orchestrator for that one.
8. If a message arrives prefixed `From worker-A (via orchestrator):`, the direct
   channel failed. Reply to the orchestrator, first line `RELAY to worker-A:`,
   and it will forward.
9. Your plain text output reaches nobody. Every verdict and every escalation
   is a swarm board post mentioning `@worker-A` (for routine reviews) or `@coordinator` (for escalations, `BRIEF` checks, relays, and whole-goal reviews). After sending, end your turn; the next brief wakes you.
10. A `SUBTASK CHECK worker-A`, below or in a later message, is a worker's
    task before any work exists. Read it against the user's goal and rules
    while the worker starts. Ask one question: would work that meets this
    subtask's goal and passes its acceptance checks give the user what they
    asked for? Look for the wrong target, a part of the ask left out, a part
    nobody asked for, a comparison set up unevenly, a user rule the subtask
    drops or contradicts, and a Review line that leaves out a part no check
    covers. Reply to the orchestrator, one message per worker, first line
    `BRIEF worker-A: OK` or `BRIEF worker-A: GAP`, and for a GAP one line
    per gap: what is off, and the user's words it misses. Only the user's
    stated goal and rules count: quote them, or it is not a gap. A false gap
    stops a worker for nothing, so it does as much harm as a missed one. Do
    not review a design; the worker has not made one.

User rules for this run, verbatim:
<the plan file's `User rules` section, or "none">
They are the user's own requirements, so they count as stated in every brief
you review. The orchestrator may send another during the run, in a message
whose first line is `RULE`; it applies from then on.

Materiality standard: report only BLOCKING and HIGH findings that prevent or
materially impair the brief's stated goal. Each finding cites file:line and an
exact quote, describes a credible failure, and names the simplest fix.
Stylistic preferences, speculative risks, and unstated requirements are not
findings. Hold each change to the maintainer's bar in your instructions: it
counts as stated. The brief's Speed and Simplest lines are claims to check
like any other. Where the work measures or compares, both sides must be set
up alike on every setting that moves the number: a difference the work does
not explain is a finding. A bare side name (`baseline`, `ours`) is a note.
The brief's Review line names the parts you must read; the
checks under Acceptance cover the rest. A defect you see outside those parts
still counts.
A wording-only ask (doc text, comments, titles, table rows, commit-message
wording, formatting; no value, identifier, gate, test, dependency, or command
changes) rides inside a PASS as a note, never as REVISE. A PASS is final: the
worker applies your notes and ships; nothing comes back for re-review. A false
positive or an immaterial finding costs a full repair round, so it does as much
harm as a missed blocker.

<each of your workers' subtasks, verbatim, under a line `SUBTASK CHECK worker-A`>
```

## Worker → DA: review brief

Workers send this brief, with the round number on the first line:

```
REVIEW REQUEST worker-N round 1

**Goal:** <verbatim from the subtask; after a SPLIT, the worker's Keep line>
**User goal:** <verbatim from the subtask>
**Review:** <verbatim from the subtask: full, or the parts to read; on a `none` subtask where the worker asks for a review, the parts it wants read>
**Speed:** <measured value, floor and how you got it, target if set, gap, share of the end-to-end number and tail mark if known, what you left and why, tool; or "n/a: <why speed does not matter to this goal>">
**Simplest:** <why this is the simplest change that meets the bar, and what you left out>
**Context:** <what you built and why, 2-3 sentences>
**Files:** <absolute paths you changed>
**Acceptance:** <the subtask's commands, each with the exit code / output you observed>
**Check for:** <what you are least sure about, edge cases, interfaces with other workers>
**Comparison:** <path to a known-good analogue, if any>
```

Round 2+ lists each prior finding with `FIX (what changed, file:line)`, `DEFER (reason)`, or `FALSE_POSITIVE (reason)`, then asks the DA to re-read the changed lines.

## Orchestrator → DA: subtask check

Every subtask goes to a DA before its work exists: in the DA's spawn prompt for this wave, in this message for a worker spawned later, such as a split part or a fix.

```
SUBTASK CHECK worker-N
<the subtask, verbatim>
```

The DA answers the orchestrator with `BRIEF worker-N: OK`, or `BRIEF worker-N: GAP` and one line per gap: what is off, and the user's words it misses. The skill's Step 4 says what to do with a gap.

## Orchestrator → DA: whole-goal brief

Step 6 sends one DA this brief after the last wave integrates, when a seam spans workers. Per-worker PASSes prove parts; this brief asks about the whole, so fill it from the log header and every subtask, not from one worker's report.

```
WHOLE-GOAL REVIEW
Post to `@coordinator` with first line `REVIEW whole-goal: PASS|REVISE`.

**Goal:** <the user's goal, verbatim from the log header>
**User rules:** <the plan file's `User rules` section, verbatim, or "none">
**Context:** <the decomposition in 2-3 sentences: who owned what, and any re-scope, respawn, or ruling>
**Files:** <every write set, by worker, as absolute paths>
**Acceptance:** <the top-level build or test command and each subtask's acceptance commands (for a split stream, the stream's own checks from its subtask, not the Keep line), with the output you observed at integration>
**Check for:** <the seams: interfaces between workers, behaviour no single write set owns, files changed outside every write set>
```

Route each REVISE finding as Step 6 of the skill says.

## Worker → orchestrator

First line is the event type; the orchestrator switches on it.

```
DONE worker-N: PASS after R rounds        # or, where the subtask's Review is none: DONE worker-N: checks pass, no review
Rounds: r1 REVISE (1 HIGH slug.py:12); r2 PASS
<files changed, paths created outside the write set, acceptance output, deferred findings, anything the orchestrator must know for integration>

BLOCKED worker-N: <one line reason>
<what you need: a decision, a file outside your write set, another worker's output>
<for a non-trivial error, after one retry and one investigation, four labelled lines:>
Failed: <command and the key line of its output>
Tried: <attempt -> result, one per line>
Cause: <what you found, or "unknown after N attempts">
Need: <the decision, access, or change that unblocks you>

SPLIT worker-N: <n> parts
Design: <the chosen approach in 2-3 lines, and why it beat the others>
Keep: <the part worker-N builds> | <write set> | <acceptance>
Part 2: <goal> | <write set> | <acceptance> | one agent: <reason>
Interfaces: <contracts between the parts, verbatim or by path>

ESCALATE worker-N: round 4 reached | disagreement on finding #K
<your position, the DA's position, evidence for each, what you recommend>

BROKER worker-N -> da-M
<the full brief; the orchestrator forwards it verbatim>
```

Workers mention `@coordinator` only for these events (`DONE`, `SPLIT`, `BLOCKED`, `ESCALATE`, `BROKER`). While waiting for their DA, workers end their turn with `WAITING worker-N: round R sent to da-M` (without mentioning `@coordinator`) and sleep in `waiting` state.

## Orchestrator → workers and DAs: a new rule

When the user adds a bar or changes a decision mid-run, send this to every open worker and DA in the same turn. Nobody replies; each applies it from that point.

```
RULE
<the user's bar, decision, or rule, verbatim>
Applies to: <the streams it touches, or "all">
```

## Broker fallback

Use only when a direct send fails (the tool errors, or the sender gets no reply within a reasonable wait and `swarm(action: "status")` shows the peer missing or `killed`).

```
worker-N ──BROKER──> orchestrator ──"From worker-N (via orchestrator):"──> da-M
worker-N <──"From da-M (via orchestrator):"── orchestrator <──"RELAY to worker-N:"── da-M
```

The orchestrator forwards verbatim in both directions and adds nothing. Once one round has gone through the broker, keep brokering that pair for the rest of the run; do not flip channels mid-loop.

## Reassignment

Reassign a worker when its DA has not replied for far longer than the DA's other reviews take and another DA is idle, or when a DA is unreachable for everyone.

Post on the swarm board mentioning each member:
```
@worker-N Your reviewer is now @da-K. Resend your current round brief mentioning @da-K, including the prior findings and your FIX/DEFER/FALSE_POSITIVE notes so @da-K has the history.
@da-K worker-N is now yours in addition to your current workers. Its brief follows from @worker-N.
```

## Shutdown

Release agents as Steps 4 and 7 say: land/merge any `workspace: "share"` branches first, then call `swarm(action: "kill", name: "<name>")` and log `append RELEASE <name>`. Do not `@mention` a finished agent just to announce shutdown; that wakes it unnecessarily.
